body: Not using WindowWrapper means the global shortcut forwarding doesn't work. So the floating window should either use WindowWrapper's ShortcutBin or we should the use the setting that will be added in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/115980.

When the floating window is closed, I would expect docks to restore back to the main window instead of being closed.
Maybe we can store the last non-floating dock slot index?
Isn't this already handled in `_move_dock`?

This makes all floating docks have the same name, which makes them harder to distinguish. 
I think we should dynamically change the title based on the selected dock. (And if we add multiple slots to a floating window in the future then whatever the last focused one was or have a main one.)
This still needs to grab focus on the window. Otherwise it may be behind another window or minimized and it will not be made visible.
This could be moved near the load function, it is only used there.

It seems strange to have a `Make Floating` button when the dock is already floating. If there is only one dock in the container, then it doesn't make sense to show. If there are multiple docks, then it can be useful, but it is already floating so it is not accurate. It could be reworded to something like "Move into New Window". We could rename it to always be worded like that actually.
Re-opening the dock from the Docks menu will restore the window. Windows are like normal slots now, except other slots can't be mass-closed.
Looks too wide. I could remove "New", but it'd probably miss the point... EDIT: Alternatively, "Detach Window", but the dock is not a window, so not sure.

Per-window icons got merged. Is it too much? 🤔

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a2cf297e-9d77-4064-b2e5-716b9beaff64
The method definitions follow order of declarations in the header, and this method is private, unlike the other load method. They can't really be near each other.
I went with title only, as icons were unreliable.
Went with "Detach Window". The tooltip explains it, so it's fine probably.
Doing the checks every time was too annoying.

It's probably more efficient to use the hash map iterator to check all existing values of `floating_slots` than to check 1000 values in it. It's not really a hot path so it isn't too important.

Now that the floating dock has a dock container, this should be the dock tab container's size instead of the dock's size. (if it is in one)
Doing this should also fix an issue when detaching a dock that was not ever switched to yet having the wrong size.

When opening a dock for the first time with a default slot of none, I get `  ERROR: editor\docks\editor_dock_manager.cpp:420 - Index p_idx = -1 is out of bounds (EditorDock::DOCK_SLOT_MAX = 11).`
with no other error. Otherwise it opens fine.

Restoring the window from the Docks menu is fine when the docks are closed from the window. 
When closing the window itself, I feel like restoring all docks to the main window is probably the most expected behavior. 
Users will already be used to closing the window to restore the dock, and restoring all is more useful than closing all too, since there is only one of each dock and you generally don't want to close most docks.
I guess if there are a lot of docks or ones designed to be temporary, then it may be better to close them, but we don't really have that info.
If the user detaches the filesystem dock or another important dock we should try to prevent the user from accidentally closing it. They can still close it directly from the context menu if they do want it closed.
That's my take on it at least, we may want to get more opinions.

Loading floating windows isn't working. When I detach a dock and restart the editor, the dock is in its default place, not detached. Same with loading layouts saved with floating windows, the docks don't move to floating windows.
This doesn't check 1000 values, unless you had opened that many windows (which is not possible, because there is not enough docks).
This won't work with bottom panel when it's collapsed.

WindowWrapper had lots of extra code for setting to a saved position that is now being skipped.
`FEATURE_SELF_FITTING_WINDOWS` is ignored.
`interface/multi_window/maximize_window` is ignored.
`screen_get_usable_rect` is never checked, resolution changes aren't handled.
etc
The drag hint doesn't show an outline when its in a floating window, which makes it look like its just a blue tint.
